changes: Fixed a candidate-layer (rule-layer) recall gap for CrowdStrike (NASDAQ:CRWD): the company registry previously only carried the automatically-generated full legal name ("CrowdStrike Holdings, Inc.") from the securities master data, not the bare company name ("CrowdStrike"/"Crowdstrike") that appears far more often in real text -- messages using the bare name never generated a candidate at all, so the classifier never had a chance to score them.

This was one item in a broader internal 5-company candidate-layer fix attempt (CrowdStrike, Nebius, Marvell, JPMorgan, Alibaba). Only CrowdStrike survived the project's evaluation discipline (frozen data, independent double-blind labeling with arbitration, pre-registered statistical gates with bootstrap confidence intervals, not just point estimates). The other four are documented below as explicitly rejected/deferred for this release, not silently dropped.

targeted_test_metrics.scope: NASDAQ:CRWD only, same classifier both sides, candidate-layer config swapped

bootstrap_ci.method: paired resampling by message, 5000 draws, one-sided 95%

deployment_observation.other_company_diff_method: same text replayed through pre-fix and post-fix candidate-layer snapshots, diffed directly -- not compared against a possibly-stale database history field

NASDAQ:NBIS.reason: Real, statistically-confirmed precision regression (CI lower bound well past the -2pp non-inferiority margin, not sample noise). Root cause: the bare word "Nebius" is used far more casually/decoratively in social text than the ticker or full company name, producing genuine false positives (personal banter, undifferentiated multi-ticker lists, repeated boilerplate) that the ticker-only matching never had.

NASDAQ:MRVL.reason: Recall point estimate positive but confidence interval lower bound did not clear 0 -- direction is right, statistical strength is not yet there at the tested sample size.

NYSE:BABA.reason: Same pattern as Marvell: positive point estimate, confidence interval lower bound did not clear 0.

NYSE:JPM.reason: Pre-fix baseline recall was already 100% on the tested sample -- no headroom for the recall-improvement gate to fire. Not evidence the fix lacks value, just that this test sample had no missed cases to recover.

pre_release_checks.config_diff_audit: passed -- diffed the candidate-layer config against the pre-fix baseline, confirmed the only change is the single new CrowdStrike row
pre_release_checks.sha256_manifest: recorded before and after, matches the deployed file
pre_release_checks.regression_tests: passed -- 3 new CrowdStrike tests in tests/test_mapper.py flip from failing (pre-fix) to passing (post-fix); full existing suite unaffected
pre_release_checks.small_scale_deployment_observation: passed -- see deployment_observation above, all 5 pre-registered conditions met
pre_release_checks.rollback_drill: rollback restores the pre-fix candidate-layer config; verification is that the 3 new regression tests flip back to failing, confirming the rollback took effect

known_limitations: This release does not change the classifier (classic-lr-v6 unchanged) -- it only affects candidate generation for one company.

Nebius/Marvell/JPMorgan/Alibaba candidate-layer fixes remain on the internal backlog; any future release covering them requires fresh data and an independently re-run acceptance protocol, not a reuse of this round's evaluation data.
